ratings_why.fun: Crowning a favourite and stacking Defers onto it is a real seating puzzle, but the Gale readers are four near-identical threshold checks and chained Gusts get hard to follow.
ratings_why.distinct: Defer, where weak courtiers hand their attack to the biggest unit of any tribe, plays unlike today's tribes and acts out the court's precedence; the Gust itself is close to familiar extra-attack text.

verdict_why: Lady High Pressure and Sir Vane don't read the way the builds use them; fix those wordings, the rest can stand.

points.text: Lady High Pressure gives Defer to every other unit, including the favourite, so the biggest never attacks normally and its turn passes to the second-biggest. Say whether the biggest is exempt, e.g. "Your other units, except your biggest, have Defer."
Sir Vane's "your side attacks first" overrides the more-units rule but says nothing about two Vanes meeting. Put the tiebreak on the card (e.g. "if both sides have this, the usual rule applies").
"Once a cycle" and "Twice a cycle" aren't in Bramble's limit words (turn, fight). Define a cycle in the Gust keyword text so the limits read at a glance.

Pine-Cone Augur, Red Sky at Night, Cirrus Steward and Mackerel Sky all read "if your Gale is N or more". Give one of them a different shape, like a forecast you set before the fight that pays if it comes true, so the readers don't blur.
The Sí Gaoithe is the fairy host passing on a still day, but its card is a high-Gale check. Paying out after a fight with few Gusts would act out the lore and give the tribe an off-day payoff.

standouts.why: Lady High Pressure stops the whole court so one wind can blow: the sovereign who forbids anything to happen, shown in what she does.
Old Föhn takes the hits for everyone else's Gusts, so he's literally blamed for everything; a clear, readable protection job.
Bowing Zephyr bows out of its turn and cheers the favourite on; one line, instantly readable, and it shows the court's manners.

weakest.why: Cirrus Steward is a generic End of Turn buff to the biggest; nothing in it says cirrus or steward.
The Sí Gaoithe has an opaque name and a dry threshold check, and the item it makes is the real card.
Pine-Cone Augur is a plain Gale-threshold stat seed; the pine-cone lore isn't in what it does.

flags.note: Unclear whether the biggest unit also gets Defer, which changes the whole Favourite build.
Two Sir Vanes in a mirror have no written ruling.
Golden Wild Hunt counts each Gust three times, so the Gale goes 18 to 21 and can skip "reaches 20". Say "reaches 20 or more".
Lord Mistral with Mistral Outrider, Windhover and Couriers makes long out-of-turn chains that may be hard to follow on screen.
Old Föhn, Lady High Pressure and The Swift Couriers together may make a favourite that never takes damage.
